rows.rule_id: PB69/body-repro — FUNCTION MOD(A ** 3, B) consumes the saturated FromDouble sentinel
rows.expected: §15.64.4 1): "The equivalent arithmetic expression is ((argument-1) – ((argument-2) * FUNCTION INTEGER ((argument-1) / (argument-2))))". With A=999999999999999, B=1000000007 that expression's value is 999999999999999**3 mod 1000000007 = 980012199 (python: A**3 = 999999999999997000000000000002999999999999999, 45 digits; A**3 % B = 980012199). §15.4.1 bounds the native-arithmetic latitude: "When native arithmetic is in effect and an equivalent arithmetic expression is specified, the value returned is an implementor-defined approximation of the value of that expression." A value derived from Int128.MaxValue is not an approximation OF THAT EXPRESSION — it is independent of the argument's magnitude, which the sibling test T4 proves (A**4, a value 10^15x larger, returns the SAME number). §15.64.1: "The MOD function returns an integer value that is argument-1 modulo argument-2."

rows.expected: §8.8.1.2 2) fixes exponentiation's place in the hierarchy so `A ** 4` and `A ** 3` are each evaluated as arithmetic expressions before the relation is tested; §15.4.1's latitude covers an implementor-defined APPROXIMATION of a value, not the collapse of two distinct values onto one sentinel. Ruled out as the source of 966729007 (python): the 28/32/34/35/36/38-significant-digit roundings of A**3 give 1012193 / 980012200, the raw double gives 842234747, and 16/17-significant-digit truncation gives 1012193 — none is 966729007, so the Dec arm takes a THIRD, unidentified approximation path.
rows.mechanism: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Intrinsics/CobolIntrinsics.RealArgs.cs#PowNativeIntDec, final line `return CobolDec.FromDouble(Math.Pow((double)b, (double)e));` — the exact Int128 loop's `fits` guard fails at 45 digits and control falls to the CobolDec double conversion, whose normalization loses the low-order digits the modulus depends on. These are of the class and category boolean." + §15.2 "the function so described may be used anywhere a sending data item of that class and category may be specified" make a BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER call's result class/category BOOLEAN. Therefore: (D2a) §8.8.4.2.8 "An operand of class boolean may be compared with another operand of class boolean" makes `IF FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER(544,6) = B"100000"` LEGAL and TRUE (§15.13.4 r1 left-truncates 544=0b1000100000 to the low 6 bits 100000). (D2b) §8.8.2 admits "an identifier referencing a boolean data item" as a boolean expression, and §15.2 lets the boolean function stand there, so `COMPUTE B8 = FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER(5,8) B-AND B"00001111"` is LEGAL and must give 00000101. (D2c) the SAME §8.8.4.2.8 sentence admits ONLY another class-boolean operand, so the alphanumeric mirror `IF FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER(5,8) = "00000101"` must be REJECTED. (D2d) §8.8.1.1 "An arithmetic expression may be an identifier referencing a numeric data item, a numeric literal..." admits only numeric operands, so `COMPUTE N = FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER(5,8) + 1` must draw a compile-time class diagnostic — never an unhandled exception. (D3) §15.50.3 r1 "Argument-1 shall be an alphanumeric, national, or boolean literal; a data item of any class or category; a based entry; or a type-name." admits the argument, and §15.50.4 r1 "the returned value is an integer equal to the length of argument-1 in boolean positions" makes `FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER(5,8))` = 8.

One rule ("a boolean intrinsic call is class/category BOOLEAN") written in five+ places, none of which has an arm for a BoundComputedOperand wrapping a BoundIntrinsicCall of ResultCategory Boolean. Confirmed present in the tree: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Validation/StatementValidation.cs#CheckRelationalOperands (line 225 — rejects the legal boolean relation with COBOLNET0844 AND admits the illegal alphanumeric/numeric mirrors in both operand orders; reached from ConditionBinder.cs:553 and from EVALUATE); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/ConditionBinder.cs#BindBoolOperandValue (line 81 — COBOLNET1511 on a legal B-AND / B-NOT operand); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/IntrinsicBinder.cs#BindLengthFold (line 1327 — routes the boolean result down the numeric-literal arm, COBOLNET1627, independent of the argument kind); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/IntrinsicBinder.cs#IsStringOperand (line 1289 — classifies the boolean call as string, so the numeric context falls through to NotImplemented.Value<T>("string-class FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER in a numeric context"), an unhandled exception at run time, exit 127). IntrinsicCatalog already maps IntrinsicType.Boolean -> PicCategory.Boolean correctly, and MOVE's Table-16 site already consumes that correctly for a computed operand — the extraction target is the classifier MOVE uses, consulted by the other five checkpoints.

The note owns NO traceability-inventory rows: a scan of all 4311 objects in E:/CobolSharp/tests/version-matrix/traceability-inventory.json for the string "PB70" returned 0 hits, so there was no inventory verdict or forensic note to read and no "rows this note owns" block exists in E:/CobolSharp/kb/Work/PB70.md. I therefore probed the note's measured repro directly plus the sibling contexts its body asks for (DISPLAY, relation operand, function argument, receiving item, STRING INTO, ACCEPT INTO).

Findings, all from cobol.exe runs I executed (default --std 2023, compiler at E:/CobolSharp/src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe, probes in E:/Temp/claude/E--CobolSharp/021d6d7d-c03e-41d0-a27a-a40839e6e4fd/scratchpad/probe-fleet/PB70/):

1. The recorded repro reproduces verbatim. `MOVE TB(1:1) TO EL(3)` with `01 TB. 05 EL PIC X OCCURS 3.` still dies with NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: reference 'TB(1:1)'.

2. The charge is NOT MOVE-specific and NOT OCCURS-specific. Any GROUP reference-modification used as a SENDING operand dies loud: MOVE source, relation-condition operand (IF TB(1:1) = "A"), DISPLAY operand, and FUNCTION ORD argument all hit the same NotImplemented.Value. A group with no OCCURS at all (01 GP. 05 GA PIC X(2). 05 GB PIC X(2. / GP(2:2)) dies identically, so the OCCURS in the original repro is incidental.

3. NEW AND STRICTLY WORSE THAN THE NOTE RECORDS - a GROUP refmod as a RECEIVING item is a SILENT WRONG ANSWER, not a loud stage. `MOVE "Z" TO TB(2:1)` compiles clean, runs to exit 0, emits zero diagnostics, and leaves TB UNCHANGED. Mechanism located: ExpressionBinder.ResolveTargets is `targets.Select(ResolveReceiving).OfType<Place>().ToList()`, and ResolveReceiving returns null for a group refmod, so the receiver is dropped from the list entirely. A multi-receiver probe proves the drop: `MOVE "Z" TO OK1 TB(2:1) OK2` moves into OK1 and OK2 and silently skips TB. The comment directly above that line (ExpressionBinder.cs:441-443) asserts this chokepoint exists so receivers are NOT "SILENTLY dropped by .OfType<Place>()" - the code is exactly that pattern and the null from the refmod gate falls straight through it. This means PB70's frontmatter is wrong: `wrong_answer: false` and `silent: false` should both be true, and severity MINOR is understated.

4. NEW - `FUNCTION LENGTH(<group>(a:b))` is REJECTED AT COMPILE TIME with a factually false diagnostic: "COBOLNET1627: FUNCTION LENGTH argument-1 is a numeric literal". The argument is a reference-modified group, not a numeric literal. The elementary control passes (FUNCTION LENGTH(EE(1:2)) prints 2), and FUNCTION LENGTH(TB) with no refmod prints 3, so the failure is specific to the group+refmod combination and the diagnostic misreports what it saw.

5. STRING ... INTO <group>(a:b) and ACCEPT <group>(a:b) FROM DATE each stage loud with their own distinct feature strings, so the receiving-side family splits: MOVE is silent, STRING/ACCEPT are loud. That inconsistency is itself evidence the null-place handling is per-verb rather than centralized.

ROOT MECHANISM (one gate, read-only inspection): E:/CobolSharp/src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/ReferenceResolver.cs lines 317-327. The refmod category gate tests `item.Pic?.Category`; a group item has `Pic == null`, so `item.Pic?.Category is not (PicCategory.Alphanumeric or PicCategory.NumericEdited or PicCategory.National or PicCategory.Boolean)` evaluates true and the method returns null. Group items are never admitted, although ISO 8.4.3.3.3 SR1 names them twice - bullet 3 "an elementary data item of category alphanumeric or an alphanumeric group item" and bullet 9 "a group item that is neither a strongly-typed group nor a variable-length group". Adding groups to that gate fixes the sending side; the receiving side additionally needs ResolveTargets to stop swallowing nulls, or fixing the gate alone will silently convert the silent no-op into correct behavior while leaving the .OfType<Place>() swallow live for the next null-returning receiver.

FIX ORDERING WARNING: fix the gate and the ResolveTargets swallow in the same change set. Fixing only the gate hides the swallow; fixing only the swallow turns the silent no-op into a loud crash without making the construct work.

PB71.note:
PB71 owns ZERO rows in tests/version-matrix/traceability-inventory.json — a grep for "PB71" across the repo hits only DEVLOG.md, docs/COBOLNET_REARCHITECTURE_PLAN.md, kb/Work/PB59.md and kb/Work/PB71.md. The note body also has no "rows this note owns" block. I therefore probed the note's own repro plus its explicit fix-time sweep list (ALL N"…", ALL NX"…", ALL B"…", ALL BX"…", ALL X"…" in MOVE source / VALUE / intrinsic argument / INSPECT operand, plus DISPLAY, STRING and relation-condition positions), and used PB71-M* / PB71-N* as rule_ids.

HEADLINE: PB71 is LIVE and is TWO defects with THREE distinct root sites, not the one the note triaged, and one member fails at the WRONG STAGE (run time, not compile time).

(a) NATIONAL — exactly as triaged, and TOTAL: `ALL N"…"` and `ALL NX"…"` fail to parse in EVERY position probed (MOVE source, VALUE clause, relation condition, INSPECT ... BY, FUNCTION argument, DISPLAY, STRING), at --std 2002, 2014 and 2023 alike. Root site: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolExpressions.g4 lines 537-552, rule `figurativeConstant`, whose arms are ALL STRINGLIT | ALL HEXLIT | ALL BOOLLIT | ALL ZERO | ALL SPACE | ALL HIGH_VALUE | ALL LOW_VALUE | ALL QUOTE_ — there is no `ALL NATLIT` and no `ALL NATHEXLIT` arm.

(b) BOOLEAN — the note guessed "the grammar's ALL production evidently admits only the alphanumeric/hex literal forms". That guess is WRONG for boolean and the truth is worse. The grammar DOES carry `ALL BOOLLIT` (g4 line 546), so `MOVE ALL B"1" TO <bit item>` compiles clean and then dies at RUN TIME with NotImplementedCobolFeatureException. Root site: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/ExpressionBinder.cs#FigurativeOperand (lines 200-211) tests `fig.STRINGLIT()` and `fig.HEXLIT()` and has NO `fig.BOOLLIT()` arm, so it falls through to `new BoundOperandError(...)`. This is verbatim the PB4 defect shape described in that method's OWN <remarks> at line 194 ("the grammar had been ready for all along ... parsed and then died at RUN time") — the same bug, one arm later, sitting directly under the comment that warns about it. Proof it is a two-arm miss and not a missing feature: ConditionBinder.BindBoolOperandValue line 96 HAS the arm (`if (fig.BOOLLIT() is { } allBl) return new BoundBoolAll(...)`), and `COMPUTE BQ = BR B-AND ALL B"1"` / `B-OR ALL BX"5"` both run and give correct values. StatementValidation.cs line 244 already pattern-matches `BoundAllLiteral { Category: PicCategory.Boolean }` — a consumer waiting on a producer that never fires, which is why the relation `IF BR = ALL B"1"` reports COBOLNET0844 instead of comparing.

(c) NEW SIBLING FAMILY found by the rule-4 sweep, NOT in the note: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs#ValidateValueCategory lines 1113-1114 compute `isNatLit`/`isBoolLit` off the RAW text and require `raw[1] is '"' or '\''`. Consequently the plain hexadecimal forms `VALUE BX"A"` on a bit item and `VALUE NX"005100510051"` on a PIC N(3) item are BOTH rejected with COBOLNET0898 — no ALL involved. Per §8.3.3.4.1/§8.3.3.5.1 those hex formats ARE boolean/national literals, so §13.18.63.3 SR10/SR5 admit them. This site will ALSO wrongly reject `VALUE ALL N"Q"` the moment the grammar arm lands, so it must be fixed in the same change set or the grammar fix will look like it worked and won't have.

SPEC BASIS (all five decisive clauses --check'd, see the citation column): §8.3.3.6.3 SR2 admits alphanumeric, boolean OR national literal-1 for Format 6; §14.9.25.4 GR7 + Table 17 assign `ALL literal` the category of literal-1 (Alphanumeric/Boolean/National); §14.9.25.3 SR10 + Table 16 make National→National and Boolean→Boolean moves valid. §8.8.2 explicitly lists "the figurative constant ALL literal, where literal is a boolean literal" as a boolean expression, and §8.8.2 formation rule 4 ("shall not BOTH be the figurative constant ALL literal") proves ALL-literal may be the FIRST operand — which is why formation rule 1's begin-list cannot be read to exclude it, and why `IF BR = ALL B"1"` (a §8.8.4.2.2 Format 2 boolean relation) is legal.

SEVERITY CORRECTION for the note: it carries severity MINOR / rejects_legal_source:true / crashes:false. The boolean-MOVE member CRASHES at run time on legal source (crashes:true), which the note does not record.

rows.expected: §15.3.3.3: "The seconds subfield of the data shall contain a value that is greater than or equal to 00 and less than 61 when the LEAP-SECOND directive with the ON phrase is in effect." With `>>LEAP-SECOND ON` in effect, "235960" is therefore a permissible seconds value, so §15.79.3 r4 ("the contents of argument-2 shall be a time in that format") is satisfied and §15.79.4 r1's equivalent arithmetic expression ((H*3600)+(M*60)+S) must yield 23*3600 + 59*60 + 60 = +86400.00. HEADLINE: the note's triage is substantially STALE. The table's SHAPE fix has largely landed — IntrinsicArgumentRules is now an ArgSchema with per-POSITION kinds, a CrossArgRule axis (AllSameClass / MatchArgument1), a noZeroLen clause slot, and an Int128-domain range guard replacing the (long) narrowing. 14 of 40 rows are FIXED, 26 remain LIVE. Every LIVE verdict below carries a compiled+run wrong/accepted output I executed.

THE FIVE PREDICATE KINDS THE NOTE NAMED, RE-MEASURED:
- INTEGRALITY of a computed operand: LANDED for data items and for nested-intrinsic/parenthesised computed operands (COBOLNET1627 now names "a numeric data item with digits to the right of the decimal point"), and §8.4.3.2.3 SR11 is now enforced where a row exists. STILL OPEN for non-integer LITERALS and for non-always-integral arithmetic EXPRESSIONS: FUNCTION MOD(11.5, 4) -> 3.5000 and FUNCTION MOD(A / 2, B) -> 2.5000 both compile clean, from an INTEGER-type function (§15.64.1).
- CROSS-ARGUMENT agreement: LANDED for MAX/MIN (§15.59.3 r2, §15.63.3 r2) and FIND-STRING (§15.37.3 r2). NOT wired to ORD-MAX/ORD-MIN (§15.71.3 r3, §15.72.3 r3) — the two-arm-dispatch scar has MOVED, not closed: the catalog literally reads ["MAX"]=Uniform('p',...,CrossArgRule.AllSameClass,...) and ["ORD-MAX"]=Uniform('p',...) with no cross rule. Also NOT wired to SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME r3 or INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE r3 (both "same TYPE as argument-1", a type not a class).
- STRONG-TYPE exclusion: STILL WHOLLY ABSENT from all four of MAX/MIN/ORD-MAX/ORD-MIN, at 2002/2023 alike. This is not a modelling gap: StrongTypeModel is live in this build (COBOLNET1533 fires on a strong MOVE receiver, positive control P58H001/P58H002), so the predicate exists and the intrinsic screen simply does not consult it.
- MINIMUM WIDTH: STILL ABSENT for §15.57.3/§15.97.3/§15.78.3 ("at least one character position") and §15.70.3 ("one character position"). The KnownWidth predicate EXISTS but is hand-wired into CheckRepertoireArgs for DISPLAY-OF/NATIONAL-OF argument-2 only — one rule, one place, still violated four ways.
- VALUE DOMAIN (§15.13.3 r1/r2): LANDED as runtime EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION with the right clause. §15.9.3 r3's positivity landed the same way; its INTEGER half did not.
- WHOLE FUNCTIONS WITH NO ROW: the date family SPLIT. INTEGER-OF-DATE and INTEGER-OF-DAY gained 'i' rows and now screen class + integrality + SR11. DATE-OF-INTEGER, DAY-OF-INTEGER, DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD and DAY-TO-YYYYDDD have NO row in Verified and none in DeliberatelyUnscreened — grep-confirmed — and screen nothing. NUMVAL and NUMVAL-F likewise have no row. CONCAT was moved into DeliberatelyUnscreened (recorded, not fixed).

THE Int128 WRAP IS DEAD — the single largest landing here. Every date/FACTORIAL repro that used to sail through the (long) narrowing now aborts: "EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal): the intrinsic integer argument <N> is outside the range the function can represent (ISO §15.3)". Confirmed on DATE-OF-INTEGER, DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD, DAY-OF-INTEGER, DAY-TO-YYYYDDD, INTEGER-OF-DATE, INTEGER-OF-DAY and FACTORIAL. The CS0117 "…Real does not exist" backend leak is also gone across the family (COMP-2 arguments now run).

TWO NEW OBSERVATIONS THE NOTE DOES NOT CARRY:
(1) The MAX/MIN r1 diagnostic still hardcodes the WRONG clause in its message body — "FUNCTION MAX argument-1 is of class boolean, which ISO §15.71.3 excludes …(§15.59.3 r1)" — two different clauses in one sentence, exactly the residue AR-15.59.3-1 predicted. REFUTATION: RV-15.59.4-3's antecedent finding rests on a FALSE PREMISE. Baseline replicated (r1base reproduces the prober's four values exactly), and the whole-item MOVE/VALUE/relation cases plus editions 85/2002/2014, group receivers, level-88 VALUE, FUNCTION LENGTH/ORD and wide-literal relations are all spec-correct. But three input variations the prober held fixed still show the defect, the strongest being a SILENT WRONG ANSWER: `ALL X"…"` is not materialized to the width of a REFERENCE-MODIFIED operand, in both a MOVE receiver and a relation operand — the two positions the claim itself enumerates. r24final is decisive: identical figurative `ALL X"5157"`, two receivers of length 3 (FUNCTION LENGTH witnesses 003), plain PIC X(3) yields the correct "QWQ" while the ref-modified 3-char receiver yields "QW ". r20width3 shows the mirror image in the relation position: A3 and A7(2:3) hold identical content and compare equal to each other, yet A3 = ALL X"5157" is EQ while A7(2:3) = ALL X"5157" is NE. Spec: §8.3.3.6.4 GR2 (repeat character by character to >= the receiver's character positions, then truncate from the right) applied to the §8.4.3.3.4 GR6 unique data item, which is an elementary fixed-length alphanumeric item of 3 character positions. Second refutation: X"…" as an INSPECT operand CRASHES at run time (NotImplementedCobolFeatureException claiming X"51" is a numeric literal) — this is verbatim the "INSPECT operand" item of PB71's own fix-time sweep, and §14.9.22.3 SR3 + §8.3.3.2.1 make X"51" an alphanumeric literal, which SR3 expressly admits; the plain-alnum control INSPECT ... FOR ALL "Q" tallies 003 correctly, so the crash is specific to the X"…" form that M7 is about. Third: `ALL X"51" & X"57"` is rejected COBOLNET1541, though §8.3.3.6.3 SR2 — the very rule the claim invokes — says literal-1 "may be a concatenation expression", and §8.8.3.2 SR1 bars an ALL-figurative only as an OPERAND, which forces the reading ALL (X"51" & X"57"); bare X"51" & X"57" without ALL compiles fine (r6catplain), so the concatenation machinery works and it is the ALL binding that mis-parses. Fourth, lesser: `ALL X""` is silently accepted (r10zerolen, r15zlvalue) where SR2 says literal-1 "shall be neither a figurative constant nor a zero-length literal", and §8.3.3.2.3 NOTE 2 makes the zero-length hexadecimal-alphanumeric literal reachable. Attribution note for the parent: the ref-mod, concatenation and zero-length failures reproduce identically with plain alphanumeric ALL literals (r9refmodctl, r5catctl, r14zlctl), so those three are general ALL-figurative defects rather than hex-specific ones — they still refute M7 as stated, because M7 asserts absolutely that ALL X"…" works in MOVE, VALUE and relation positions. PB63.note:
Adversarial refute of 7 PB63 "FIXED" claims against the prebuilt Debug cobol.exe at E:/CobolSharp/src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe (HEAD a6f5d610). 27 probe programs, all with unique PROGRAM-IDs, all under E:/Temp/claude/E--CobolSharp/021d6d7d-c03e-41d0-a27a-a40839e6e4fd/scratchpad/probe-fleet/PB63-refute/. No repo file touched, no build, no test suite.

CITATIONS I VALIDATED MYSELF (cite.py --check, all OK): 8.4.3.2.3 SR1 "A function-identifier shall not be specified as a receiving operand."; SR2 "the word FUNCTION may be omitted from the function-identifier"; SR6 "If a function's definition permits arguments and a left parenthesis immediately follows"; SR8 "Argument-1 shall be an identifier, a literal, a boolean expression, or an arithmetic expression."; 8.4.3.1.2 "Format 1 (function-identifier)"; 8.4.3.2.4 GR5b "BY CONTENT is assumed ... or any identifier that is not permitted as a receiving operand."; 12.3.4 GR1 "The entries explicitly or implicitly specified in the configuration section of a source unit that contains other source units apply to each directly or indirectly contained source unit."; 15.32.3 r2 "the returned value is a 63-character alphanumeric character-string that is the name of the statement"; 15.33.3 r1 "A 31-character, left-justified, alphanumeric character string that is the exception-name"; 15.65.4 r1 "an alphanumeric dynamic length elementary item with no trailing spaces".

TWO CLAIMS BROKEN, both by ONE newly-measured mechanism: a string-class function-identifier passed as argument-1 of a USER-DEFINED function compiles with NO diagnostic and then dies at run time with NotImplementedCobolFeatureException "string-class FUNCTION <name> in a numeric context" - the exact silent-mis-compile signature PB63 was opened for. It reproduces for EXCEPTION-STATEMENT, EXCEPTION-STATUS and EXCEPTION-LOCATION, with the FUNCTION keyword and with the SR2 keyword-omitted form, with a numeric-returning AND an alphanumeric-returning callee. Isolation (r3h) shows a plain PIC X(63) item in the same slot works and FUNCTION UPPER-CASE fails identically, so the root cause is a SHARED channel gap (every string-class intrinsic in a user-defined-function argument list), not an exception-family defect - route it accordingly. 8.4.3.2.4 GR5b names precisely this shape ("any identifier that is not permitted as a receiving operand"), so the source is legal.

SIDE FINDINGS OUTSIDE THE SEVEN CLAIMS (not scored, but measured):
(a) UNDER-REJECT of 12.3.8.3 SR13. r1e.cob: `REPOSITORY. FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC.` together with `01 EXCEPTION-LOCATION PIC X(5) VALUE "DATA!".` compiles clean and prints `L=[DATA!]`. SR13 says "If ALL is specified ... none of the names of the intrinsic functions may be specified as a user-defined word within the scope of this REPOSITORY paragraph" - a diagnostic is required. The new SR2 resolver silently lets the data item win.
(b) COSMETIC: diagnostic COBOLNET1632 renders the name as 'FUNCTIONEXCEPTION-STATEMENT' (missing space). Its clause cites (14.9.22.2 / 14.9.22.4 / 8.4.3.2.3 SR1) are correct - 14.9.22 is INSPECT in this transcription.
(c) UNPROBEABLE AXIS: r5's fourth activation mechanism, an INLINE INVOCATION, cannot be exercised - `P63R6BC::"WHOACT"` is a hard parse error (r6b.cob: `error COBOL0001: no viable alternative at input ':'`); `::` is absent from the grammar entirely (grep of src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar returns no DOUBLECOLON/inlineInvocation). RV-15.65.4-5 therefore cannot diverge on that mechanism in any runnable program, but it is not positively verified either.

design.summary: Drafted the complete LOCALE-facility deep-dive at E:/Temp/claude/E--CobolSharp/021d6d7d-c03e-41d0-a27a-a40839e6e4fd/scratchpad/probe-fleet/PB64-design/DESIGN-locale-facility.md (1116 lines, repo-target docs/rearchitecture/DESIGN-locale-facility.md), covering all thirteen Annex A.4.9 items plus the two rules the module reaches into that no A.4.9 item names (figurative HIGH-VALUE/LOW-VALUE under a locale PCS, §8.3.3.6.4 GR6/7, and CHAR/ORD positions, §15.15.4 r1 / §15.70.4 r1). Every semantic claim carries a cite.py --check-validated clause (~130 runs; six PICTURE locale rules the first pass wrote as §13.18.40.4 FAILED and are §13.18.40.5 Editing rules, and the figurative rules are §8.3.3.6.4 not §8.3.3.6 — both corrections recorded in the doc so they are not re-inherited; the printed index was rejected as a source since it points EC-LOCALE-SIZE at 13.18.36/LOWLIGHT). §1 is fourteen MEASURED rows of literal cobol.exe output, which materially updates the PB64 triage: the SPECIAL-NAMES LOCALE clause and the LOWER-/UPPER-CASE LOCALE phrase now draw a correct named COBOLNET1518 (PB25 landed), but OBJECT-COMPUTER CHARACTER CLASSIFICATION is still SILENTLY accepted at 2023 AND at --std 85 (an A.4.1 violation under the current non-support posture too), CHARACTER CLASSIFICATION after PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE is a parse error though §5.2.6.4's choice indicators make either order legal, SET LOCALE draws three misleading diagnostics, save-locale and PICTURE format 2 are raw parse errors, and ALPHABET IS LOCALE is refused with a miscited COBOLNET0901/0898. A fifteenth finding fell out of the grammar work and is NOT a locale defect: OBJECT-COMPUTER with computer-name-1 omitted is rejected (COBOL0001) though §12.3.6.4 GR3 provides for its absence — the doc routes it to its own kb/Work note rather than housing it. The design specifies one LocaleSymbol/LocaleRef compile-time model, one RunUnit-owned LocaleState (with the §14.6.6 r9 rule that a callee's switch is NOT unwound), a saved-locale managed handle table for the data-pointer formats, and the load-bearing restructuring: CobolString.Compare's three overload carriers collapse into ONE CobolCollation abstraction because §8.8.4.2.11 comparison is an algorithm with no padding, not a weight table — plus ten numbered ⚖ DETERMINATIONs (external-locale-name → normalized BCP-47, the two defaults with env overrides for golden reproducibility, no foreign-switch visibility, the handle model, one sequence for both classes, when EC-LOCALE-INCOMPATIBLE fires, the ORD/CHAR order vector, indexed keys, simple case mapping as ISO-9945-equivalent, d_fmt/t_fmt), a full CultureInfo/ICU mapping table with its documented limits (invariant-globalization mode, NLS-vs-ICU, ICU skew, no int_frac_digits carrier, generated pattern→placement table), seven constructs.json edition rows at 2002 with the mandatory gate sweep, a COBOLNET1642+ diagnostic band, a seven-increment migration whose T0 posture repair is owed under EITHER answer to the implement-vs-non-support question, and a test plan built around what each test would catch. The GnuCOBOL survey is split [M]/[U]: cobc is not installed here, so the only measured facts are the four harvested testsuite cases (LOCALE-COMPARE accepted with the one-character "<"/">"/"=" contract pinned, LOCALE-DATE/-TIME/-TIME-FROM-SECONDS accepted with non-blank-only assertions) plus their WE_REJECT_THEY_ACCEPT differential verdicts that will flip on landing; STANDARD-COMPARE, SET LOCALE, PICTURE format 2, CHARACTER CLASSIFICATION and the SPECIAL-NAMES clause have NO GnuCOBOL evidence in-repo and every claim about them is marked UNVERIFIED.
open_questions: Q1 (OWNER-RESERVED) — Does COBOL.NET claim A.4.9 support at all? Ratified council decision 3 (2026-07-03) dispositions the locale module to documented non-support, which is conforming per §4.2.7 + A.4.1; this design specifies the full implementation because CLAUDE.md rule 3 forbids scoping a design to the current posture, but adopting it REVERSES a ratified owner decision. Note track T0 (posture repair) is owed under EITHER answer: today's behaviour is not the non-support posture — it is an A.4.1 violation (CHARACTER CLASSIFICATION silently accepted, measured at 2023 and --std 85) plus outright rejection of legal source (clause ordering, measured).

Q2 (OWNER-RESERVED) — Are COBOL_USER_LOCALE / COBOL_SYSTEM_LOCALE env vars the right implementor mechanism for §8.2.1's two 'the implementor shall specify the manner in which the user/system default locale is defined' duties, or should the defaults come from a compiler option or a runtime configuration file so the mechanism is visible in the compile command? DETERMINATION L2 proposes env vars because golden tests must be reproducible on any host.

Q3 (OWNER-RESERVED) — Should a locale-based collating sequence be offered for INDEXED file primary/alternate keys? §A.3 item 41 makes it processor-dependent, so BOTH answers conform. DETERMINATION L8 proposes yes, with the documented caveat that a file written under one locale and read under another is not guaranteed to be in key order.

Q4 (OWNER-RESERVED) — STANDARD-COMPARE / ORDER TABLE and ISO/IEC 14651:2020 (A.4.9 item 11 + A.3 item 25): (a) acquire and ship the default ordering table 'ISO 14651_2020_TABLE1', (b) claim .NET's ICU root collation as a logically-equivalent implementation of it, or (c) keep A.3 item 25 non-support but with a CORRECT named diagnostic. This is a data-acquisition and conformance-claim decision, not a design decision; the design is written for all three and increment T7 is gated on the answer.

Not owner-reserved, answerable by measurement: the five GnuCOBOL [U] rows in §9 — whether GnuCOBOL accepts the SPECIAL-NAMES LOCALE clause, SET LOCALE formats 11/12, PICTURE format 2 (locale) and OBJECT-COMPUTER CHARACTER CLASSIFICATION. cobc is not installed on this machine (`where cobc` returns nothing) and the harvested corpus is silent on all four, so no latitude decision may lean on them until they are re-derived from GnuCOBOL's documentation (never its GPL sources).

Not owner-reserved, a spec reading that should be settled before increment T3: whether §8.3.3.6.4 GR6/GR7's 'the character, OR MULTIPLE-CHARACTER COMBINATION, that has the highest/lowest ordinal position' has any realizable meaning for HIGH-VALUE/LOW-VALUE in a typed-native one-character figurative constant, or is an artefact of byte-oriented implementations. §4.4.4 assumes the latter and returns a single character with a code-unit tie-break.

Not owner-reserved, but an unverified determination that must fire in a test before it is trusted: DETERMINATION L6 — when EC-LOCALE-INCOMPATIBLE (§8.8.4.2.11 sentence 3) can actually be raised, given that ICU assigns an implicit weight to every unassigned code point so no culture literally 'fails to define a collating sequence'. The doc proposes unpaired surrogates and noncharacters and requires a golden that observes the condition, because a registered-but-never-raised EC is a dead lookup.

Provisional and explicitly NOT re-litigated here: the 2002 vs 2014 edition windows for the locale intrinsics. The 2023 text proves only presence-in-2014 (Annex E lists no locale addition) and says nothing about 2002; ratified decision #1 forbids further standards acquisition, so the seven new constructs.json rows inherit the neighbouring rows' provisional 2002 marking rather than asserting it.

design.summary: Drafted the complete deep-dive for the EXTERNAL FLOATING-POINT PICTURE category — which the 2023 standard actually calls a **floating-point numeric-edited item** (§13.18.40.4 GR13 b; "external floating-point" has 0 occurrences in the spec, so the doc retires the term). PB66 owns two inventory rows, RV-15.43.4-1 and RV-15.58.4-1, both NOT-IMPLEMENTED/GAP because the construct itself cannot be declared; I confirmed the LIVE rejection with executed runs (`PIC -9.9(5)E+99` → `COBOLNET0899 … recognized but not yet implemented` at --std 2023, `COBOLNET0900 … requires COBOL-2002` at --std 85, and both ALGEBRAIC folds falling to `COBOLNET1516`), plus a baseline run proving the fixed-point fold over the spec's own `PIC $**,**9.99BCR` example already answers correctly (HI=[0000999999I] / LO=[0000999999R]), and an eight-mask probe proving the LEXER AND GRAMMAR NEED NO WORK — every `E` picture reaches PictureAnalyzer intact. The design settles: storage stays the existing numeric-edited `string` image (the category IS numeric-edited, class alphanumeric per §8.5.2.1 Table 2 — no new PicCategory, no new CLR carrier); the legal symbol alphabet is derived from Table 10 row `E` **re-read off the rendered PDF page 490** (only `B 0 /`, `,`, `.`, a leftmost fixed `+`/`-`, and `9` may precede `E` — so no V, P, S, Z, *, cs, CR/DB, or EDITING character-1), and the rendered row matches the Markdown transcription cell-for-cell; Annex A.3's latitude for >31-digit significands and >3-digit exponents is proven INAPPLICABLE to this implementation (its antecedent requires no standard-float support, and COBOL.NET has FLOAT-BINARY-32/64 plus STANDARD-DECIMAL), which forces the full 1–36 / 1–4 range and therefore an EXACT DECIMAL value channel — reusing the existing `CobolDec(Int128 Sig, int Exp)` and the existing `NumX.Dec` lane rather than `double`, which would lose 19 of 36 digits. Form dispatch is moved INTO `RuntimeApi.EditFormat`/`EditTryFormat`/`NumericRenderer.FieldNum` so none of the six call sites can forget it; the MOVE-vs-arithmetic divergence on out-of-range stores (§14.9.25.4 GR6 4a/4b treats underflow as zero, §14.7.5 cases 3/4 raise SIZE ERROR) is wired as an explicit two-arm hazard with goldens on both sides; and the two owned rules become a compile-time well-formedness test at the function reference whose bound is parameterised by the arithmetic mode (binary64 under NATIVE ⇒ `E+9`/`E+99` pass, `E+999`/`E+9999` fail; decimal128 under STANDARD-DECIMAL ⇒ the line moves to `E+9999`). Sixty-plus clause citations were validated with `scripts/spec/cite.py --check`; one FAILED and was corrected in the ledger (§12.3.7 → §12.3.7.3 SR22 b) — the same inherited-citation shape RV-15.58.4-1's own note records. Two concrete defects surfaced: `DataBinder.cs:2147` routes every numeric-edited item through the SR14 31-digit cap, which would wrongly reject a legal 36-digit significand, and `constructs.json`'s `pic-external-float-2002` row carries an ILLEGAL sample picture (`PIC +9V99E+99` — V may not precede E), which would make the edition-gate test pass for the wrong reason.
open_questions: Q1 — OWNER-RESERVED. What deterministic content does a floating-point numeric-edited receiver hold after the §14.9.25.4 GR6 4a overflow case, which the standard leaves UNDEFINED while setting EC-DATA-OVERFLOW? The design proposes the SATURATED extreme image (all-nines significand at the maximum exponent, value's sign preserved) as decision D-EF8. Alternatives: leave the item unchanged (one rule shared with the arithmetic SIZE ERROR arm, but MOVE has no unchanged tradition and it hides the overflow from a program that ignores the EC), or the §13.18.40.5 rule-8 zero image (symmetric with the underflow arm, but it turns a huge value into zero — the worst wrong answer). This ships as a pinned behaviour determination in docs/CONFORMANCE.md, so it is an owner call.

Q2 — INTERPRETIVE, recommendation given. BLANK WHEN ZERO (§13.18.8.4 GR1: zero ⇒ all spaces) versus §13.18.40.5 rule 8 (zero ⇒ all significand and exponent digits zero, both signs positive). Both are stated unconditionally; the standard states the precedence only for the LOCALE format (§13.18.40.5 rule 10, 'A BLANK WHEN ZERO clause takes precedence over locale editing'). Recommendation: BLANK WHEN ZERO wins — GR1 is specific to the clause's presence, rule 10 is the sibling precedent, and it matches what CobolEdit.Format already does for every fixed-point edited mask. Rejecting BLANK WHEN ZERO on such an entry is the only alternative and would reject source §13.18.8.3 SR1 plainly admits.

Q3 — OWNER-RESERVED. Should COBOLNET1648 (the §15.43.4 r1 / §15.58.4 r1 range test) also fire at the DECLARATION, not only at a HIGHEST-/LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC reference? As designed it fires only at the function reference, because that is the only place the rules constrain, and a `PIC 9.9E+9999` item is otherwise perfectly usable (no legal sender can produce a value that large, so no store can overflow it). Warning at declaration is friendlier but flags source the standard permits.

Q4 — INTERPRETIVE, recommendation given. Is a significand with NO decimal point (`PIC 999E+99`) legal? GR13 b requires the significand to be 'a valid character-string for either a numeric item or a numeric-edited item for a fixed-point result'; `999` is a valid numeric character-string and Table 10 row E admits `9` before `E`. Note the deliberate asymmetry with a floating-point LITERAL, where §8.3.3.3.3 r2 explicitly requires the significand to include a decimal point. Recommendation: legal, SigScale = 0 — flagged because a reader will assume the asymmetry is a mistake.

Q5 — SCOPE, needs its own kb/Work note rather than a decision here. The EXISTING fixed-point `CobolEdit.DeEdit` never raises EC-DATA-INCOMPATIBLE: §14.6.13.2 rule 4 applies to every numeric-edited sender whose content 'is not a possible result for any editing operation in that data item', but the implementation silently contributes zero for any non-digit (CobolEdit.cs:284). This design adds the check on the FLOAT path only; fixing the fixed-point twin touches every existing edited golden and must not be smuggled into this wave.

Q6 — SCOPE. USAGE NATIONAL with a floating-point edited picture: §13.18.40.4 GR1 makes every symbol a national character position and §8.5.2.1 Table 2 makes the item class NATIONAL. COBOL.NET already stages the whole national-form numeric/numeric-edited family loud (PictureAnalyzer.cs:210, Phase-4a residue). The design inherits that existing, already-tracked stage rather than fixing it — but the wave must CONFIRM the float form actually takes that stage and does not slip through it.
